subject: Orbit Health: streaming client/parser fragmentation causing latency + errors
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbithealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production errors - Redwood SDK streaming

Mina / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in error rates and long tail response latency from our integration that uses the Redwood JS SDK (streaming path). Started ~05:00 UTC yesterday and has persisted intermittently. Symptoms: 20-30% of streaming responses terminate with a protocol error on the client, and a sizable fraction (>10%) of requests take 2-3x our normal p95 latency.

We've attached a small sample log and an HTTP Archive capture from a reproduction attempt. The errors look like: "parser: unexpected header boundary" and repeated client retries. The spike correlates with a traffic increase but reproduces on a single request from our staging host.

This is impacting our user sessions (live transcription flows). We need an urgent path to stabilize — either a short-term config/workaround or a patch ETA. Please advise next steps.

Sam Turner
Head of Integrations, Orbit Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production errors - Redwood SDK streaming

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. We're prioritizing this. A few quick asks so we can triage faster:

- Can you confirm SDK version in production (package.json / yarn.lock)?
- Any proxy/load-balancer between your client and our endpoint?
- If you can reproduce reliably, please include a HAR for a failing session (you already attached one — thanks).

Immediate mitigations to try while we investigate:
- If you can toggle the SDK to non-streaming (polling/batched) mode, it should avoid the parsing path hitting the bug.
- If not, increase client retry backoff to 5s to reduce retry storm and lower tail latency.

I've looped in Rishi from the runtime team and Marissa from CS. We'll follow up within 2 hours with initial findings. Apologies for the disruption — we'll get you a containment plan shortly.

— Mina
Director, Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production errors - Redwood SDK streaming

Quick engineering summary from an initial repro (thanks for the HAR and logs):

Findings:
- Root cause appears to be a boundary-handling bug in the Redwood JS client streaming parser (v1.4.2 and v1.4.3). When the server emits chunked frame headers that split across TCP packets (rare, but present under certain proxies), the SDK's incremental header parser can mis-detect the header delimiter and drop the remainder of the message. That triggers a protocol error on the client and causes client-side retries; retries plus backoff interaction amplifies observed p95 tail.
- The server-side traces show our runtime completed the request in ~220ms, but client-side saw repeated partial reads and retries leading to 1.8s+ end-to-end in affected sessions.

Immediate mitigation (what we can do in the next 2-4 hours):
- Patch and hotfix the client parser to reassemble split header boundaries (we have a minimal fix; attaching repro_minimal_patch.diff). We can provide a patched SDK build for you to test within 3 hours.
- Server-side fallback: allow tolerant parsing on our streaming edge to accept header fragments that don't strictly match the previous framing when the client indicates older SDK versions. We'll roll a conservative inbound relax flag to reduce protocol errors; this will be deployed to a small percentage of edge capacity in ~2 hours.

Longer-term: put robust fuzzing and chunk-boundary tests into the CI for all client SDKs and add a server-side compatibility matrix.

Action items assigned:
- Rishi: prepare patched SDK build and test matrix (ETA 3h).
- Marissa: coordinate a staged rollout with Orbit (customer-facing comms + temporary credits if needed).
- Mina: own executive updates and postmortem once stabilized.

I'll push a reproducible branch and the patch to INF-4728.

— Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jon ASVP <jon@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit Health - executive escalation and remediation prioritization

Folks — brief summary for leadership:
- Impact: Orbit Health (live transcription) experiencing elevated error rates and p95 latency due to client SDK streaming parser failing on fragmented chunk headers. Customer revenue impact moderate; they are reporting user session failures.
- Risk: If not contained, retries could escalate to wider edge congestion and affect neighboring tenants in the same pool.

Requests:
1) Prioritize the tolerant-edge fallback and the SDK quick patch. Engineering should treat this as Sev-2 until mitigated.
2) Offer Orbit a corrective credit (recommendation: 30% of the last billing cycle for measurable user-impacted requests) and a dedicated weekly update until full RCA. CS to confirm exact amount.
3) Prepare a one-page exec summary for the next leadership sync. Mina, please lead.

Marissa — please coordinate the credit/communication plan with Account and Finance. Rishi — let me know if you need code review bandwidth or infra rollback support.

— Sean
Head of Customer Success (interim)
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit Health - interim fix and next steps (INF-4728)

Sam — update and plan: thanks again for the artifacts and patience. We've validated the reproducer and confirmed the SDK parser bug as the proximate cause. Next steps and timeline: 

1) Immediate containment (now): Marissa has enabled a communications channel and Finance is standing by to review credit options. For a short-term containment you can: set the SDK config flag `streaming: false` (client-side) or add header `X-Redwood-Stream: poll` to avoid the streaming path. This avoids the parser entirely.

2) Hotfix & rollout (ETA 3 hours): Rishi will deliver a patched SDK build (v1.4.4-hotfix) and we will deploy a tolerant parsing fallback to 10% of streaming edge capacity to reduce errors while you test the build. We'll expand to 50% after a successful 1-hour canary.

3) Follow-up & RCA (ETA 72 hours): full postmortem and CI tests (INF-4728) plus a plan for permanent server-side hardening.

Attachments: orbit_errors_0516.log, har_capture_0516.har, repro_minimal_patch.diff.

We regret the disruption — we'll commit to daily status updates until fully resolved. Please confirm whether you want us to push the hotfix build to your staging environment for validation.

— Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
